articles.title: Gurugram Woman Arrested After Viral Video Shows Domestic Help Being Assaulted Inside Luxury Apartmen
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Gurugram)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.caption: Gurugram
articles.excerpt: A 52-year-old woman was arrested in Gurugram after a viral video allegedly showed her assaulting her domestic help inside a luxury apartment in Sector 42. Police took suo motu cognisance, registered an FIR and released the accused on police bail as the investigation continues.

body.html:
A 52-year-old woman was arrested by Gurugram Police after a nearly 90-second video allegedly showing her assaulting her domestic help inside a luxury apartment in Sector 42 went viral on social media.

The accused, identified as Ruchira Sachdeva, a resident of DLF The Camellias, was allegedly involved in an argument with the domestic worker over work-related issues on July 24. The video, reportedly recorded by a neighbour through a kitchen window, shows the woman allegedly pulling the domestic help by her hair, slapping her, striking her with a mobile phone and pushing her during the confrontation.

Police took suo motu cognisance of the viral footage and began an investigation. An FIR was registered at Sushant Lok police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including Section 115(2) for voluntarily causing hurt and Section 127(2) concerning wrongful confinement.

Police said the domestic help, a Nepalese national who had worked at Sachdeva's home for around two years, left the job on July 27 and subsequently returned to her hometown.

According to police sources, the woman has not filed a complaint and reportedly submitted a written statement requesting that the video be removed from social media. A relative also told police that she had no grievance against her former employer.

Despite the absence of a complaint from the domestic worker, police proceeded on the basis of the viral footage. Officials visited the location and conducted a field inquiry.

DCP (East) Sandeep Kumar said the facts surrounding the incident and the video were being verified and that action would be taken according to law.

Sachdeva joined the investigation after her arrest and was later released on police bail, according to officials. The case has been forwarded to senior officials and the area magistrate, while further investigation continues.

articles.title: Allahabad HC Calls Meerut Woman’s Arrest ‘Illegal’, Orders Release Within 24 Hours
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Uttar Pradesh)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Allahabad High Court has declared the arrest and custody of Rimisha, accused of murdering her sister-in-law Nida in Meerut, illegal, citing alleged procedural lapses in the arrest record. The court directed her release within 24 hours while the murder case continues.

body.html:
The Allahabad High Court has declared the arrest and subsequent custody of Rimisha, accused of murdering her sister-in-law Nida in Meerut, illegal and directed that she be released within 24 hours.

Rimisha was arrested by Lisari Gate police on July 12 from her home. Her lawyer alleged that she was kept at the police station for nearly two days before being produced before a court on July 14.

During proceedings, the defence sought CCTV footage from the police station to establish the circumstances and timing of her arrest. Police reportedly claimed that the CCTV cameras were not functioning and that no recording was available.

The High Court, while examining the arrest records, reportedly found discrepancies in the arrest memo. The court noted that the arrest time appeared to have been overwritten and that several mandatory columns, including those relating to witnesses, were left blank.

Considering the alleged procedural violations, the court held the arrest, custody and remand to be illegal and directed the Chief Judicial Magistrate in Meerut to ensure Rimisha's release within 24 hours.

Rimisha is accused of fatally stabbing Nida with a kitchen knife during an alleged domestic dispute.

According to the prosecution's allegations, Nida was allegedly involved in a relationship with Uwais, who was a friend of her husband. Police allege that around eight months before the killing, Nida manipulated circumstances that resulted in Uwais marrying Rimisha, her sister-in-law.

After the marriage, Rimisha allegedly discovered that her husband was involved in a relationship with Nida. This reportedly led to a confrontation between the two women in the kitchen, during which Rimisha allegedly attacked Nida with a knife, causing her death.

The High Court's order concerns the legality of Rimisha's arrest and custody and does not amount to a finding that she was innocent of the murder allegation. The criminal case itself remains subject to further proceedings.

articles.title: Hospital Ceiling Collapses on Woman at Rajasthan Government Hospital, Patient Narrowly Escapes Death
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Rajasthan)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman was injured after ceiling plaster and part of a concrete canopy collapsed at the entrance of a government maternal and child hospital in Sujangarh, Rajasthan. CCTV footage captured the incident, raising concerns over the safety and maintenance of the hospital building.

body.html:
A woman was injured after a portion of the ceiling plaster and concrete canopy collapsed at the entrance of the Government Fatehpuriya Maternal and Child Hospital (Zenana Hospital) in Sujangarh, Rajasthan's Churu district.

The incident, which was captured on CCTV, occurred at the hospital's main entrance when part of the ceiling suddenly gave way and fell on the patient.

The woman sustained a head injury in the incident and required two stitches. She narrowly escaped what could have been a fatal accident.

The collapse has raised serious concerns over the condition of the government hospital building. According to reports, warnings had previously been issued about the deteriorating state of the structure, highlighting long-standing concerns over its safety.

The CCTV footage of the incident has since surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the alleged poor maintenance of public healthcare infrastructure.

articles.title: Wife’s Body Found Stuffed in Suitcase: Husband Arrested 1,500 Km Away After 2 Months on the Run
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Uttar Pradesh)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.caption: The victim Chhoti Upadhyay, the accused Rishabh Kumar Singh
articles.excerpt: A man accused of murdering his wife and hiding her body inside a suitcase in Silvassa was arrested nearly 1,500 km away in Varanasi, where police allege he lived under a false identity and worked as a labourer. He is being taken back to Silvassa for investigation.

body.html:
A man accused of murdering his wife and hiding her body inside a suitcase in Silvassa was arrested nearly 1,500 km away in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, after allegedly living under a false identity.

Rishabh Kumar Singh, a native of Nawada, Bihar, was arrested on Monday by a joint team of the Varanasi STF and Silvassa Police from the Chandpur Industrial Estate in the Manduadih area.

According to police, Rishabh had married Chhoti Upadhyay, a woman from his village, against his family's wishes. Police said tensions arose after his family allegedly refused to accept Chhoti as their daughter-in-law, while she reportedly pressured him to take her to his family home.

Investigators allege that amid the dispute, Rishabh murdered Chhoti inside their rented accommodation in Silvassa on June 9 and concealed her body inside a suitcase before fleeing.

The case came to light on August 3, when a landlord opened the locked room in the Tokar Khada area of Silvassa after planning to rent it out. A foul smell led to the discovery of a suitcase containing a decomposed body wrapped in plastic. The deceased was subsequently identified as Chhoti Upadhyay.

Police said Rishabh fled Silvassa after the alleged murder and eventually took shelter in Varanasi. He reportedly worked as a labourer at Chandpur Industrial Estate using the assumed name Kamlesh.

The STF began tracking him after information about his whereabouts emerged through a phone number reportedly shared with an acquaintance. Police eventually located and arrested him from a rented accommodation in the Manduadih area.

During interrogation, police also learned that a kidnapping case had previously been registered in Bihar's Roh police station in connection with the couple.

Rishabh was produced before the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court in Varanasi, where Silvassa Police obtained transit remand. He is now being taken to Silvassa for further investigation and legal proceedings.

Police are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding Chhoti's alleged murder, the motive and whether anyone else was involved.

articles.title: Road Rage Erupts on Pune Street: Drivers Brawl in Middle of Busy Road, Traffic Comes to a Halt
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Maharashtra)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A road rage incident on Pune’s busy Koregaon Park–Mundhwa Road escalated into a physical fight between two motorists, briefly disrupting traffic. A video of the confrontation has surfaced online, while details of any injuries or police action remain unavailable.

body.html:
A road rage incident was reported on Pune's busy Koregaon Park–Mundhwa Road, where a verbal altercation between two motorists escalated into a physical fight, disrupting traffic and drawing the attention of passersby.

According to eyewitnesses, the incident began when the driver of a white Scorpio, reportedly on the way to a CNG station for refuelling, got into an argument with the driver of a navy blue car.

The dispute is believed to have stemmed from road space and the right of way amid heavy traffic congestion. As tempers flared, the verbal exchange quickly turned into a physical confrontation in the middle of the road.

The fight briefly brought traffic to a standstill as bystanders gathered at the scene. A video of the incident has since surfaced on social media.

No official information regarding injuries or police action was immediately available.

The incident has once again highlighted the growing number of road rage cases in urban areas, where traffic congestion and commuting stress are increasingly leading to violent confrontations. Authorities continue to urge motorists to remain calm, avoid arguments, and resolve disputes peacefully.

articles.title: Bareilly Gym Fight Takes Ugly Turn: Third-Gender Person Allegedly Stripped, Assaulted and Subjected
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Uttar Pradesh)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.caption: Sushil Kumar and Ashwani Sharma
articles.excerpt: A dispute over alleged car vandalism outside a gym in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, escalated into a violent confrontation. A third-gender person and companions alleged assault, indecent behaviour, stripping and a forced gender check. Police have registered a case and detained several people.

body.html:
A dispute over the alleged vandalism of a car outside a gym in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, escalated into a violent confrontation, with a third-gender person and companions alleging assault, indecent behaviour and being stripped and subjected to a forced gender check.

The incident reportedly took place outside Helios Gym in Rampur Garden and came to light after a video of the confrontation went viral on social media.

Salman alias Mannu Suri, a resident of Kohadapir who identifies as a third-gender person, said her adopted brother Vishal informed her on the morning of August 7 that his car had allegedly been vandalised outside the gym.

Mannu went to the gym and spoke to its operator, Ashwani Sharma, who reportedly said he had no information about the incident. Mannu then returned.

Later, at around 10 pm, Mannu said a friend informed her that the gym operator had claimed information had been received about the person who allegedly vandalised the car. Mannu returned to the gym with her friends.

According to her allegation, Sushil, Ankit, Ajay and others, along with Ashwani Sharma, were present at the gym. She alleged that the group behaved indecently with them and assaulted her when she resisted.

Mannu further alleged that other members of the local third-gender community subsequently arrived and that she and her companions were assaulted. She claimed that they were stripped and subjected to a forced gender check and were beaten after allegedly being declared male.

The allegations also include an accusation of attempted murder against Mannu, though the circumstances and individual roles are being investigated by police.

After the video surfaced online, Kotwali Police initiated action.

CO First Ashutosh Shivam said a case has been registered against gym operator Ashwani Sharma, along with other named and unidentified individuals. Ashwani and several others have been detained for questioning.

Police are investigating the allegations and examining the viral video and other evidence to establish what happened during the confrontation.

articles.title: Teacher Wife Found Dead in Tub in UP: Husband Accused of Murder
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Uttar Pradesh)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 29-year-old assistant teacher was allegedly murdered by her husband inside their rented home in Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh. Police suspect an attempt was made to stage the death as an accident or suicide. The husband fled and remains under investigation.

body.html:
A 29-year-old assistant teacher was allegedly murdered by her husband inside their rented home in Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday morning, with police investigating allegations that the crime was staged to look like an accident or s**.

The deceased has been identified as Shanili (Shalini) Yadav. Her husband, Dilip Kumar Yadav, an assistant teacher at a primary school in Chak Alipur, has been named as the accused in a case registered on the complaint of the woman's father, Dharam Raj Yadav.

The incident took place in the Nasirpir locality under Sadar Kotwali. According to police, the couple had an argument at around 9 am, which allegedly escalated into a physical confrontation. Dilip is accused of taking a sharp-edged weapon from the kitchen and repeatedly attacking his wife.

Shanili reportedly suffered serious injuries and collapsed. When neighbours reached the house after hearing screams, Dilip had allegedly fled the spot.

Police took Shanili to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared her dead.

According to the police case, Dilip allegedly placed Shanili's body in a tub in an attempt to make the incident appear like a s*e or accidental death.

A post-mortem examination conducted by a panel of doctors on Saturday night reportedly found three injury marks on Shanili's head and injuries on her right leg.

The couple's seven-year-old son, Darshit Singh, was present with relatives after the incident. He reportedly told family members that his parents frequently quarrelled.

According to Darshit, Dilip returned home the previous evening while Shanili was speaking to someone on the phone. He allegedly told the boy to go to his grandmother's house, saying, "We will fix your mother." The allegation is being examined as part of the investigation.

Shanili's mother, Phulmati, alleged that Dilip had conspired with his brothers, Sandeep and Bhupendra, who are also teachers, to kill her daughter. Police have yet to establish these allegations, and their alleged involvement will depend on the investigation.

Phulmati also claimed that Dilip called her on Saturday morning and told her that Shanili had been injured after falling into a tub. When she reached the house with relatives, she allegedly found her daughter dead and Dilip sitting beside the body.

Shanili's father alleged that the couple frequently quarrelled over Dilip's alleged affair with another woman.

Police are currently searching for Dilip and questioning the named accused while examining other evidence. Investigators said the post-mortem findings and further evidence will help establish the motive and the exact sequence of events.

articles.title: Woman, Lover Allegedly Kidnap 3-Year-Old Daughter; Brave 12-Year-Old Dragged 50 Metres
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Punjab)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A CCTV video from Punjab's Ludhiana allegedly shows a woman and her companion taking away her three-year-old daughter, while a 12-year-old girl was dragged nearly 50 metres trying to stop them. Police are examining the footage amid an ongoing custody dispute between the parents.

body.html:
A shocking CCTV video from Punjab's Ludhiana has surfaced showing a woman and her alleged lover forcibly taking away her three-year-old daughter in broad daylight, while a 12-year-old girl was allegedly dragged nearly 50 metres after trying to stop them.

The incident took place on July 28 on Daba Road. According to police, the accused arrived on a white scooter with their faces covered. The woman allegedly snatched her three-year-old daughter while the child was on her way to a nearby shop with her 12-year-old cousin, Anuradha.

When Anuradha tried to stop them, the woman allegedly slapped and pushed her. As the scooter sped away, the girl held on in an attempt to rescue her cousin but was dragged for around 50 metres, suffering injuries to her arms and legs. The entire incident was captured on CCTV.

The victim's father, Yuvraj Singh, told police that he married Seema Rani around 10 years ago. He alleged that she had been living separately with her lover for the past six months, leaving behind their two children—a seven-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter.

According to Yuvraj, divorce and other legal proceedings between the couple are pending. He claimed his wife wanted custody of their daughter and had allegedly threatened him over maintenance and property-related issues. He further alleged that she was using the child to strengthen her maintenance claim in court. These allegations have not been independently verified.

Anuradha told police that she was taking her younger cousin to a shop when the accused intercepted them. She alleged that when she tried to save the child, she was assaulted and dragged by the scooter.

Daba Police Station SHO Jatinder Kumar said CCTV footage is being examined and the new complaint is being added to an existing case involving disputes between the couple. Police said no final court order has been passed regarding the custody of the children, and further legal action will be taken in accordance with the law.

articles.title: Major Security Breach at India-Nepal Border: Car Smashes Rupaidiha Checkpost Barrier
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major security breach was reported at the India-Nepal border in Bahraich after a car allegedly smashed through barriers at the Rupaidiha ICP and fled. Police later found the vehicle abandoned and are probing the driver, motive and possible security lapses.

body.html:
A major security breach was reported at the India-Nepal border in Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, after a car allegedly smashed through security barriers at the Integrated Check Post (ICP) in Rupaidiha and fled the area.

The incident took place at around 3 pm on August 9 near the Rupaidiha ICP/Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI) campus. The car, bearing registration number UP 40 AR 7224, allegedly rammed the security barrier and speed gate before entering the restricted premises.

According to officials, Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) and LPAI personnel attempted to stop the vehicle and close the gate. However, the driver allegedly broke through the speed gate and escaped at high speed.

The ICP's security advisor lodged a complaint with Rupaidiha Police Station, following which an FIR was registered against the unidentified driver. Police said the driver allegedly attempted to run over personnel while escaping, and a motorcycle was also damaged during the incident.

Police and security agencies immediately alerted several police stations and outposts along the border. Personnel were deployed on highways and major roads for nearly three hours to trace the vehicle.

Authorities are examining CCTV footage from the ICP, nearby establishments and roads to determine why the vehicle entered the restricted area and to identify the driver.

According to police, the vehicle was later reportedly found abandoned between Nanpara and Matera. Police have taken it into custody and are investigating its ownership and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Rupaidiha SHO Harendra Kumar Mishra said efforts are underway to identify the vehicle owner and other persons involved using the registration number. Further details will emerge after the suspects are traced and questioned.

The incident has raised serious security concerns, particularly as the Rupaidiha border remains a sensitive transit point. Security agencies are also examining the incident in light of recent arrests at the border, including six people reportedly detained a few days earlier while crossing the Rupaidiha border.

The exact motive behind the vehicle's entry into the restricted ICP premises has not yet been established, and the investigation is continuing.

articles.title: 'Is This Mid-Day Meal?' Viral Video of Watery Curry and Burnt Chapatis Served to UP Students
articles.category: National News > State, City & Local News (Uttar Pradesh)
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A primary school headmistress in Uttar Pradesh’s Sitapur has been suspended and a cook terminated after a viral video showed students allegedly being served watery vegetable curry and poor-quality mid-day meals. Police also registered an FIR over alleged irregularities.

body.html:
The education department in Uttar Pradesh's Sitapur district has suspended a primary school headmistress and terminated the services of a cook after a video showing students being served allegedly poor-quality mid-day meals went viral on social media.

The video purportedly shows children being served watery vegetable curry with chunks of potato floating in it. The footage also shows rotis falling on the floor, after which a student reportedly picks one up and places it back on the plate.

The incident was traced to a primary school in Chhangapur village under Mahmoodabad block.

Following the circulation of the video, the Block Education Officer (BEO) Udaimani Patel and Mahmoodabad Block Development Officer were directed to conduct a preliminary inquiry. They visited the school and spoke to students and villagers before confirming that the video was genuine.

The inquiry report was submitted to Sitapur District Magistrate Dr Rajaganapathy R and Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Gorakhnath Patel.

Officials held school headmistress Kalpana Verma and cook Aneeta responsible for failing to serve food and milk according to prescribed mid-day meal norms and for preparing poor-quality food despite supplies being provided on time.

The BSA subsequently ordered Verma's immediate suspension, while Aneeta, who was employed on a contractual basis, was terminated from service.

The BEO was also held responsible for alleged dereliction of duty, and an adverse entry was made in his service record.

Police also registered an FIR against the headmistress and cook at Mahmoodabad Police Station late Wednesday evening. According to police, the FIR was filed on the BEO's complaint over allegations including embezzlement of government-supplied food material and corrupt practices.

Further action is underway.
